    Training config reference: the brewslm.yaml manifest

    After this reference you can read a brewslm.yaml manifest section by section, identify which knob controls which behaviour, and know which fields apply actually writes versus only carries.

    Level: intermediate Read time: ~11 min Type: Reference Verified: 12 Nov 2026

    Track 3's narrative lessons described what BrewSLM does. This reference describes how a project is configured at the schema level. The canonical artifact is brewslm.yaml — a project-as-code manifest the platform reads, validates, diffs, and applies. It captures the project-level settings a run starts from; per-run hyperparameters are set on the Train form and stored on each run, not in this file. Knowing its sections gives you the keys to the platform. In the workspace you get the file from Settings → Export the project manifest (or Ship → Package → Options → manifest); many fields mirror workspace settings, and each section below says where.

    Manifest envelope

    Every brewslm.yaml opens with a fixed envelope:

    api_version: brewslm/v1
kind: Project
metadata:
  name: my-project
  description: "..."
  labels: { team: "ml", env: "dev" }
spec:
  # ten sections, all optional; blueprint defaults to null, the rest to defaults

    The schema is strict-extra-forbid: unknown keys fail validation. Typos and stale fields are caught by validate / diff / apply, not as silent no-ops. Schema drift is therefore visible by design.

    One caution before the sections: a valid field is not always an applied field. Apply writes some fields to the project and only carries others (they validate and round-trip through export, but apply never reads them). Each section below marks its fields applied or carried, not applied.

    spec.workflow — project-level toggles

    Cross-cutting settings that don't belong to any single stage.

    workflow:
  beginner_mode: true
  pipeline_stage: ingestion
  target_profile_id: vllm_server
  training_preferred_plan_profile: balanced   # safe | balanced | max_quality
  gate_policy: {}
  budget_settings: {}

    All six fields are applied to the project.

    • training_preferred_plan_profile is the hyperparameter preset for the next launch, and the only plan-profile field apply reads. Three values: safe (conservative), balanced (default; right for most projects), max_quality (longer training, more aggressive knobs).
    • target_profile_id defines the export/deploy target shape — vllm_server, mobile_cpu, edge_gpu, etc. Validate rejects an unregistered id.
    • beginner_mode is the Settings → Workspace → Start advanced sections collapsed switch (default true): power tools open on request, nothing is hidden. (The Coach notices have their own switch, Show inline tips, which is not a manifest field.)

    spec.blueprint — domain blueprint

    The "what is this project actually for" section — what the + New Project dialog's "What problem do you want this model to solve?" answer becomes. Optional, but if you fill it in, the Coach notices and the auto-suggested pass/fail rules use the structured intent.

    blueprint:
  domain_name: "Customer support"
  problem_statement: "Classify intent of inbound tickets"
  target_user_persona: "Tier-1 agents"
  task_family: instruction_sft
  input_modality: text
  expected_output_schema: { ... }
  expected_output_examples: [ ... ]
  safety_compliance_notes: []
  deployment_target_constraints: { ... }
  success_metrics:
    - { metric_id: macro_f1, label: "Intent macro F1", target: "min 0.90" }
  glossary:
    - { term: "P1", plain_language: "Highest-priority ticket", category: "ops" }
  confidence_score: 0.0
  unresolved_assumptions: []
  version: 3                        # informational
  source: manual                    # informational

    Applied when present: apply validates the section and saves it as a new active blueprint revision. version and source are carried, not applied (provenance only). If you leave blueprint out (its default is null), apply leaves the project's blueprint alone. It anchors reviews ("did the model actually do what we said it should?") and feeds the eval-pack auto-suggestions.

    spec.domain — domain pack + profile

    domain:
  pack_id: customer-support
  profile_id: ticket-intent

    A domain pack ships pre-built defaults (synth playbooks, eval prompts, blueprint hints) for a vertical. Profiles narrow further. Both are pointers, and both are applied: the platform resolves them on apply. In the workspace: Settings → Tools → Domain Packs / Domain Profiles.

    spec.model — base model selection

    model:
  base_model: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct
  cache_fingerprint: "sha256:..."
  source_ref: "hf:..."
  registry_id: 42

    Only base_model is applied. registry_id is informational and re-resolved from base_model; cache_fingerprint and source_ref are carried, not applied (the exported manifest writes only base_model). Changing base_model in the manifest is a real change — apply will note it and your next training run will start from a different base. It is the Base model field at the top of the Train form (Browse opens the registry; the same list is Train → More options → Base model registry).

    spec.data_sources — registered datasets

    data_sources:
  - name: tickets-train
    type: jsonl
    description: "Q3 labeled tickets"
    record_count: 4812
    file_path: data/projects/3/sources/tickets-train.jsonl
    metadata: { schema_hash: "..." }
    versions:
      - { version: 1, record_count: 4812, file_path: "..." }

    Applied, matched by name. A new name creates the dataset, and its versions entries are written only then. For an existing name, apply updates type, description, record_count, file_path and metadata; versions is not re-applied. Apply never deletes a dataset that is missing from the manifest; it lists it as a warning. Sources are added under Data → Sources; the dataset versions panel sits in Data → Split → Details.

    spec.adapters — Adapter Studio entries

    adapters:
  - name: ticket-extractor
    version: 1
    status: active
    base_adapter_id: default-canonical
    task_profile: instruction_sft
    source_type: raw
    source_ref: "..."
    field_mapping: { input: question, output: answer }
    adapter_config: { ... }
    output_contract: { ... }

    Adapters are the data-transformation layer between raw rows and the training-ready shape. The schema is intentionally open (adapter_config + output_contract are free-form dicts) because the adapter class is what defines the contract. Applied, matched by name: an adapter version is immutable, so a changed config writes a new row at the next version (version is only used when the adapter is first created). Adapter Studio is Train → More options → Adapter Studio; the preset a split uses is picked on Data → Split.

    spec.training_plan — mostly carried, not applied

    The name suggests this section drives the trainer. Today it mostly does not: apply reads only config, and even that is not a hyperparameter set. The run itself is configured on the Train form: the task / recipe under Task → Change (= More options → Task type), the numbers under More options → Model and hyperparameters and LoRA and advanced training, preset patches under Training presets, a rented GPU under Cloud burst. Those values live on each run's own config, not in the manifest.

    training_plan:
  training_mode: sft                # default sft; carried, not applied
  plan_profile: balanced            # carried, not applied
  preferred_runtime_id: null        # default null; carried, not applied
  config: { ... }                   # applied: stored as the project's dataset adapter preset
    • training_mode (carried, not applied). A run's own mode is one of sft (default), domain_pretrain, dpo or orpo. Distillation is not in that list. The training script does understand training_mode: distillation (offline knowledge distillation against captured teacher logprobs; Track 4, Lesson 4.3 — the alpha*CE + (1-alpha)*T^2*KL loss), and the offline KD recipes (recipe.kd.*) set it together with distillation_offline: true. But the experiment API on main accepts only the four values: a create request carrying training_mode: distillation is rejected, and distillation_offline is not a field it keeps, so offline KD is not reachable through a normal run today. What does work is the live-teacher form: an sft run with distillation_enabled: true and a distillation_teacher_model.
    • plan_profile (carried, not applied). The profile apply uses comes from workflow.training_preferred_plan_profile; export fills plan_profile from that same project field. The named profile is chosen by the Autopilot Planner (Settings → Tools → Autopilot Planner); the Train form edits the resolved knobs directly.
    • preferred_runtime_id (carried, not applied; default null). The registered runtime ids are builtin.simulate (tests) and builtin.external_celery (real training through a Celery worker). A run picks its runtime from its own training_runtime_id config key; auto falls back to the server's TRAINING_BACKEND setting.
    • config (applied) is a flat dict written as-is to the project's dataset adapter preset (keys such as adapter_id, adapter_config, field_mapping, task_profile). Apply does not validate it against TrainingConfig, and it holds no learning rate or epochs.

    Where the actual hyperparameter values live

    Not in the manifest. Learning rate, batch size, epochs, LoRA r/alpha/dropout, target modules, scheduler, warmup and precision are resolved when you launch a run and stored on that run's config. Change them in Train → More options → Model and hyperparameters / LoRA and advanced training — the confirm dialog before Launch shows the resolved config. To change the project's default preset through the manifest, edit workflow.training_preferred_plan_profile, not training_plan.plan_profile.

    spec.eval_pack — what counts as "good"

    eval_pack:
  pack_id: evalpack.general.default
  datasets: [gold_dev, gold_test]
  eval_types: [exact_match, f1, hallucination, safety]
  extra: {}

    pack_id is applied (validated against the registered packs, stored as the project's preferred pack). datasets, eval_types and extra are carried, not applied: editing them changes nothing about which sets are scored or which scorers run. The pack referenced here declares the gates — in the UI the pass/fail rules (rule set) on Results → Verdict (Lesson 3.13's reference). Default datasets are gold_dev + gold_test — the platform's names for the answer key's practice and final halves, kept under Data → Labels; test is the prepared split's test examples.

    spec.export — artifact production

    export:
  formats: []                       # default; carried, not applied
  quantization: null
  extra: {}

    The whole section is carried, not applied: apply never reads it, and an exported manifest always carries an empty export section. Export formats are chosen per export, in the New export form on Ship → Package (formats offered there: GGUF, ONNX, HuggingFace, TensorRT-LLM, Docker).

    spec.deployment — endpoint target hints

    deployment:
  target_profile_id: vllm_server
  extra: {}

    Carried, not applied. Export fills target_profile_id here from the project's target profile, but apply only reads workflow.target_profile_id; this copy and extra are never applied (a diff still lists a change to them). Deployments are created and watched under Ship → Deploy / Ship → Monitor.

    What apply does with all of this

    The manifest apply service takes the parsed brewslm.yaml plus the project's current state and produces a ManifestApplyPlan — a list of ManifestApplyAction rows, each declaring a target (project / blueprint / data_source / adapter / training_plan), an operation, the before/after, and the fields that changed. The schema allows delete, but apply never emits it: deletes are intentionally not part of the apply contract, and a dataset or adapter missing from the manifest becomes a warning. Every unknown key is rejected, but a known field can still be ignored: the fields marked carried, not applied above validate, round-trip and may show in the diff, yet apply does not write them.

    Key idea

    brewslm.yaml is the catalog of every knob a project has. Read it section by section and you have read the platform's training contract. The schema is versioned (api_version: brewslm/v1) and strict (unknown keys are errors) — when the contract evolves, the next apply tells you. Strict about keys is not the same as applied: check the applied / carried marks before you rely on an edit. Edit by hand for surgical overrides; let the platform regenerate for ordinary changes.

    The next reference catalogues the audit-spine surfaces that watch what apply triggers: the RunEvent taxonomy and the Coach action catalogue behind the inline Coach notices.

    Key terms

    brewslm.yaml
    The project-as-code manifest. Versioned (brewslm/v1), strict-extra-forbid, validates / diffs / applies against project state.
    Manifest spec sections
    The ten sections of spec: workflow, blueprint, domain, model, data_sources, adapters, training_plan, eval_pack, export, deployment.
    Training plan profile
    Named hyperparameter preset — safe / balanced / max_quality. Apply reads it from workflow.training_preferred_plan_profile; training_plan.plan_profile is carried, not applied.
    Training mode
    A run's mode: sft (default), domain_pretrain, dpo or orpo; not distillation (the offline KD recipes set it, but the experiment API rejects it today; live-teacher KD is an sft run with distillation_enabled). The manifest's training_plan.training_mode is carried, not applied.
    Eval pack id
    Registered pack reference like evalpack.general.default; the pack declares the gates — the pass/fail rules shown on Results → Verdict (Lesson 3.13).
    ManifestApplyPlan
    The before/after action list produced by manifest diff / apply — create / update / noop actions (apply never deletes), every unknown key rejected.
